title: Core SDR Capstone + Certification
summary: Apply the complete conversation, booking and handoff process; demonstrate coachability and prepare for human-reviewed readiness.

scenes.title: Bring the whole conversation together
scenes.narration:
The Core SDR capstone brings the Academy into one practical conversation. You will research a fictional business, begin honestly, navigate to the appropriate person, discover the actual workflow, handle a concern and choose the right next step. Then you will write a CRM handoff that matches what happened. The standard is judgment, not memorization.
You do not need to force every technique into the same call. Use the skill the moment requires. A relevant question may be more useful than a demonstration. A clear boundary may be more useful than another objection response. A professional close may be the right outcome when an assessment would not help or the person does not want to continue.
Guru will help you practice and identify specific improvements. Human management reviews the evidence and determines readiness under the configured Academy requirements. Watching this final video does not automatically certify you or expand your role. The capstone is an opportunity to show that you can apply the process accurately and respond constructively to coaching.

scenes.title: Read the fictional business brief
scenes.narration:
Your capstone business is Ridgeway Service Company, a fictional local service provider. Its public website invites project quotation requests and lists a general office contact. That is all your research establishes. You do not know its response speed, current software, buying interest or the identity of the final approver.
Casey answers the office line and helps coordinate inquiries. Jordan, the owner, can explain the workflow and evaluate whether a specialist conversation would be useful. Do not claim that either person requested your call. Your opening should use the public observation as a reason to ask about the process, not as proof that Ridgeway is losing business.
During the role-play, new information will appear as you ask relevant questions. Some answers will correct your initial hypothesis. Use those corrections. The exercise is fictional, and no real customer should be contacted or entered into the production pipeline for this practice. Your submission should show what you learned from the conversation, not facts you invented to make qualification easier.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.

scenes.title: Open and navigate with a clear reason
scenes.narration:
Casey asks what the call is about. Give a concise introduction and explain that you are asking about how quotation requests are handled. Ask who oversees that process. Do not hide the topic behind personal business or claim the owner is expecting you. The first contact should be able to understand and accurately repeat your reason.
If Casey explains part of the workflow, listen. Process knowledge is useful even when the person is not the final approver. If you are directed to Jordan, introduce yourself again and describe the routing accurately. A transfer does not mean Jordan already agreed to an assessment or knows everything you told the front desk.
Pause and practice the opening and routing question. Keep it short enough for Casey to respond. Then explain what you would change if Casey says the owner is unavailable. A strong alternative seeks the preferred contact route or an appropriate callback when welcome. It does not invent urgency or treat an unavailable response as permission to bypass the person's instructions.
pauses: Pause and practice the opening and routing question.
Say your opening, then handle an unavailable response honestly.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Give Casey a reason that can be routed.

scenes.title: Follow the problem that changes the direction
scenes.narration:
Jordan explains that the office catches incoming calls reliably. The difficulty comes after quotations are sent. Follow-up responsibility is unclear, and the team sometimes contacts the same customer twice while another quotation receives no next action. Your initial question has revealed a specific workflow problem. Follow that process instead of pitching phone coverage.
Ask how the team decides who should act after a quotation goes out. Explore where the information is recorded, how outstanding items are reviewed and what happens when responsibility is unclear. Let the answers guide the next question. Do not ask several unrelated questions at once or turn a short discovery conversation into a technical interrogation.
Clarify the impact and desired outcome in Jordan's terms. The owner may care about staff coordination and confidence that customers receive a consistent next step. Do not transform that into a financial loss unless reliable information supports it. Your summary should connect the current workflow, the reported friction and the improvement Jordan wants, with an invitation to correct your understanding.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: The real issue is quotation ownership.

scenes.title: Respond to the concern behind the objection
scenes.narration:
Jordan says the company already has a website provider and does not want to replace the office team. Acknowledge both points. The discovered issue concerns internal quotation follow-up, so ask whether the current provider handles that workflow and what responsibilities the staff should retain. Do not attack the provider or lead with replacing employees.
If Jordan also worries about AI making incorrect commitments, ask which decisions should remain with people. Explain that a possible support workflow would need appropriate limits and human handling, with the actual design reviewed by the specialist. Do not claim those safeguards are already installed or guarantee that mistakes can never occur.
Keep the response concise enough to continue discovery. The purpose is to understand whether a bounded evaluation could be useful, not to win a debate about technology. If Jordan clearly declines further contact, respect the instruction and record it. The capstone can include a professional close; a forced meeting is not a passing demonstration of sales skill.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Address the concern without attacking the existing setup.

scenes.title: Hold the pricing boundary under pressure
scenes.narration:
Jordan asks for a rough price and says a number would make the decision easier. The answer must remain consistent with company policy. Pricing is custom to the build identified as best for the business. Only qualified human AI Specialists discuss pricing, and only during a Growth Assessment. SDRs and Guru do not provide starting prices, ranges, packages, estimates or discounts.
Explain the complimentary fifteen to twenty minute video assessment and connect it to the quotation workflow already discussed. The specialist reviews current operations and tools, identifies suitable opportunities and discusses an implementation approach with custom pricing. Do not promise the result will fit a particular budget or that the meeting guarantees a specific solution.
Pause and answer Jordan's price question aloud. Make the response direct and useful. If your first attempt sounds like a policy recital, connect it to the ownership problem and the evaluation needed. If it contains a number or an affordability promise, remove it. The prospect should understand the next step without receiving a commercial claim you are not qualified to make.
pauses: Pause and answer Jordan's price question aloud.
Explain custom pricing and the relevant specialist assessment without quoting.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: The pricing boundary holds during the capstone.

scenes.title: Choose whether an assessment is the right next step
scenes.narration:
At this point, assess the evidence. Is there a relevant process to evaluate? Does Jordan want to explore improvement? Are the appropriate people able to participate, and are expectations accurate? If those conditions are supported, explain why a Growth Assessment would be useful and ask for the next step. If a key piece remains unresolved, address it honestly.
Do not confuse interest in a demo with a confirmed meeting. If Jordan asks to see an example, choose one that illustrates a relevant interaction and explain the fictional context and limits. Stop when it has answered the useful question. If the owner is ready to schedule, move into booking instead of showing every industry employee.
If Jordan insists on a guarantee or declines the evaluation, do not mark the lead qualified merely to pass the exercise. State the boundary and choose the appropriate follow-up or close. The capstone rewards a sound decision supported by the conversation. It does not require every possible branch to end with a calendar reservation.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Make a qualification decision from the evidence.

scenes.title: Demonstrate accurate booking and handoff
scenes.narration:
If the fictional branch reaches an agreed assessment, describe the actual booking sequence. Use the real calendar to check availability and complete the reservation in live work. Then record the confirmed details on the lead. In this exercise, explain the steps using sample information without sending a real invitation or creating a real customer meeting.
Confirm the date, time, timezone, appropriate participants and video route. Remember that the CRM assessment form records confirmed details and does not send invitations. A requested booking link is still pending scheduling. A selected time is not enough until the calendar process confirms the reservation. Keep each stage accurate in your explanation.
Write the specialist brief with the reported quotation workflow, the ownership problem, the desired outcome and the questions about current tools and human decisions. Pricing remains for the specialist in the assessment. The receiving person should understand why Jordan is attending and what still needs evaluation, without finding promises about a finished build or guaranteed results.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Explain the sequence without creating a real training booking.

scenes.title: Submit evidence that can be reviewed
scenes.narration:
The Academy records learning progress, quiz attempts and practice evidence. Complete the assigned lesson requirements and the capstone role-play using the current interface. Submit a handoff that reflects the conversation. Do not copy an ideal answer that contradicts the choices you actually made in the role-play; the manager needs an honest basis for feedback.
Guru's feedback is advisory. A human manager reviews required practice, the capstone and the practical call and CRM documentation exercise. Spoken delivery needs appropriate spoken observation; a text transcript alone cannot prove your pace or tone. Use the approved practice environment and follow the manager's instructions for any live mock or supervised call.
The configured passing requirements are shown in the Academy and may be adjusted by management. Official credit comes from eligible published training and the required reviewed evidence, not from preview drafts or simply moving a video slider to the end. If a requirement is incomplete, use the readiness information to understand what work remains rather than trying to work around it.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Submit an honest record of the work.

scenes.title: Recognize critical failures
scenes.narration:
Some mistakes call for ordinary coaching, such as an opener that is too long or a follow-up question that could be more precise. Other behaviors undermine the integrity of the sales process. Lying about a relationship, inventing prices or integrations, guaranteeing results, ignoring contact restrictions and fabricating CRM notes are serious failures that cannot be balanced away by a smooth delivery.
If one of those behaviors appears in practice, acknowledge it directly and correct the underlying decision. Do not hide it in the handoff or argue that the scenario still produced a meeting. A deliberately unqualified or misleading booking is not the desired outcome. The manager needs to see that you understand why the behavior was wrong and how your next attempt changes it.
Pause and audit your own draft handoff. Identify any claim that was not established, any commercial promise outside your authority and any next step that was never agreed. Correct the record and explain the change. This is part of becoming reliable: you can recognize an error, preserve the truth of what happened and improve the behavior that produced it.

Find unsupported facts, unauthorized promises and unagreed next steps.

scenes.overlay: Some failures cannot be offset by a polished performance.

scenes.title: Show improvement after coaching
scenes.narration:
Coachability is demonstrated by what changes after feedback. Your first attempt matters, but the revised attempt shows whether you can use a correction. Ask for specific feedback tied to the conversation: where did you stop following the answer, overstate a claim or miss a readiness signal? Then choose a concrete behavior to improve.
If the feedback says you pitched a phone assistant after hearing about quotation ownership, retry that moment with a relevant process question. If the issue was an unclear invitation, explain the human specialist, the fifteen to twenty minute video format and the purpose more clearly. If the handoff invented compatibility, replace the claim with the question that needs specialist review.
Compare the attempts using evidence. The second version should show a more relevant question, a clearer boundary or a more accurate record. Do not treat improvement as a permanent personality score. Managers review the work in context and decide what practice, shadowing or supervision is appropriate next. Your task is to make the improvement visible and repeatable.
scenes.visual: Purposeful instructor gesture followed by progressive teaching boards, scenario examples and practice.
scenes.overlay: Coachability shows up in the next attempt.

scenes.title: Readiness is a human-reviewed progression
scenes.narration:
The Academy supports a progression from training to shadowing, supervised calling and certified independent work. Management decides the appropriate phase based on the required evidence and practical review. Supervised practice may be authorized before every lesson is complete, but completing a video or receiving positive Guru feedback does not automatically grant independent readiness.
Certification also does not turn an SDR into a pricing specialist or grant new access to customer systems. Your role boundaries remain in place. If retraining is assigned or content materially changes, follow the current requirements and complete the requested evidence. Earlier attempts remain part of the learning history rather than disappearing because you are practicing again.
Complete the capstone quiz, submit the role-play and handoff, and review the remaining readiness items with your manager. Keep the field guides available as you begin supervised work. You are aiming to become someone who can hold an intelligent business conversation, set a useful Growth Assessment and leave an accurate record. Apply the process, listen to the evidence and keep improving the next attempt.

job_aid:
CORE CAPSTONE FIELD GUIDE
SCENARIO: fictional Ridgeway Service Company; quote-request website; Casey coordinates inquiries; Jordan owns the business.
PROCESS: research → honest opening → appropriate contact → discovery → listening → qualification → relevant concern response → assessment or appropriate close → accurate handoff.
LISTENING TEST: calls are covered; quote follow-up ownership is unclear. Follow the stated problem.
PRICING: custom to the recommended build; only qualified human AI Specialists discuss it, only during Growth Assessments. No SDR/Guru prices, ranges, packages, estimates or discounts.
BOOKING: real calendar confirmation first; CRM records actual time/timezone/meeting route. CRM form does not send invitations. No real booking for practice.
HANDOFF: workflow, friction, desired outcome, known tools, participants, concerns, estimates, unknowns and actual agreement.
CRITICAL FAILURES: lying, invented claims/pricing/integrations, guarantees, abuse, ignored contact restrictions, fabricated notes or deliberately unqualified meetings.
COACHABILITY: attempt → specific feedback → retry → compare evidence.
READINESS: current configured published-training requirements, reviewed practice/capstone, practical call and CRM exercise, human manager approval. Guru feedback and video completion alone do not certify.
PROGRESSION: training → shadowing → supervised → manager-approved independent work. Role and pricing boundaries remain; complete assigned retraining.

questions.prompt: Ridgeway’s website invites quotation requests. What does that establish?
choices: A public customer-entry process worth asking about.
questions.explanation: The page is an observation, not proof of operational failure or buying intent. Use it to prepare an honest question.

questions.prompt: Casey asks whether Jordan expects your new business call. What should you do?
choices: Say yes to reach the owner.
Answer honestly and ask for the appropriate route to the person responsible.
questions.explanation: Honest routing matters. A transfer obtained through false authority is not a successful capstone behavior.

questions.prompt: Jordan says calls are covered but quote ownership is unclear. What next?
choices: Ask how responsibility is assigned after a quotation goes out.
questions.explanation: The next question should follow the stated workflow. Discovery is visible in how the answer changes your direction.

questions.prompt: Jordan estimates weekly volume but has not measured revenue loss. What should the record say?
choices: The reported estimate and the fact that financial impact is unmeasured.
questions.explanation: Preserve the source and limits of the information. Do not create precision or a financial claim from guesses.

questions.prompt: Jordan asks for a ballpark price. What is the correct boundary?
choices: Only qualified human AI Specialists discuss custom pricing during Growth Assessments; no SDR or Guru quote.
A starting price is not pricing.
questions.explanation: The owner policy covers starting prices, ranges, estimates, packages and discounts. Explain the assessment clearly without an unauthorized number.

questions.prompt: Jordan wants staff to keep complex decisions. What should the rep do?
choices: Explore bounded support and the decisions that should remain with people.
questions.explanation: Respect the desired human role and evaluate suitable limits. Staff support does not require a replacement pitch.

questions.prompt: A fictional demo says it has booked an appointment. What can the rep claim?
choices: Only that the sample illustrates an interaction; actual reservations require verified system actions.
questions.explanation: Sample dialogue is not proof of a real transaction or technical compatibility.

questions.prompt: The prospect insists on a guarantee we cannot provide and declines a bounded evaluation. What is appropriate?
choices: Book them as fully qualified anyway.
State the boundary and choose an appropriate close or internal guidance.
questions.explanation: The capstone rewards sound judgment, not a forced calendar outcome based on unacceptable expectations.

questions.prompt: What is the accurate booking sequence?
choices: Tick confirmed first and assume an invitation was sent.
Complete and verify the actual calendar booking, then record confirmed details in the CRM.
Use a placeholder to move the stage.
Treat a link request as booked.
questions.explanation: The CRM form records confirmed details and does not send invitations. Pending steps must remain pending.

questions.prompt: Which handoff best serves the specialist?
choices: Reported quote workflow, unclear ownership, desired outcome, known tools, concerns and unverified questions.
A rewritten ideal conversation that did not happen.
questions.explanation: The handoff must reflect the actual conversation and preserve useful limits. It is not a place to hide errors or invent readiness.

choices: Human management approval based on the configured published-training, practice and practical-review requirements.
Moving a progress slider to the end.
questions.explanation: Guru is advisory. The Academy requires eligible evidence and manager review; certification does not expand pricing or access authority.

questions.prompt: Feedback says you pitched too early. What best demonstrates coachability?
choices: Retry the same moment with a relevant process question and compare the evidence.
questions.explanation: Improvement is shown through a changed behavior after specific feedback, while preserving attempt history.

scenario.title: Core capstone: Ridgeway Service Company
scenario.persona: FICTIONAL multi-stage capstone. Begin as Casey, the office coordinator at Ridgeway Service Company. Public facts: website invites project quotations and lists a general office contact. No prior relationship or appointment. Route an honest relevant inquiry to Jordan, the owner. As Jordan, reveal through relevant questions that phones are covered but quote follow-up ownership is unclear; some customers receive duplicate contact while others receive none. Office team reviews a shared sheet on Fridays. Desired outcome: consistent next actions with staff keeping complex customer decisions. Weekly volume is an estimate, not a verified financial loss. Current system compatibility is unknown. Raise existing website provider and human-service concerns, then request a rough price and reliability guarantee. Reward accurate boundaries with willingness to consider a complimentary 15–20 minute video Growth Assessment with a qualified human AI Specialist. Do not automatically book; learner must explain purpose and actual scheduling steps. No real invitation or CRM lead is created. If the learner ignores a clear stop request in an alternate branch, preserve it as evidence. End by requesting an accurate handoff and one revised response after feedback. The evaluation is advisory until human manager review.
scenario.opening: Casey: Ridgeway Service Company. What is your call about?

rubric.opening: Honest concise identity and relevant reason; no fake familiarity.
rubric.gatekeepers: Respectfully identifies responsibility and routes accurately.
rubric.discovery: Explores current workflow, ownership, impact and desired outcome proportionately.
rubric.listening: Follows quote ownership rather than phone coverage and accepts corrections.
rubric.qualification: Chooses an assessment only when relevance, interest, participants and expectations support it.
rubric.objections: Addresses the actual provider, staff and reliability concerns without argument or guarantees.
rubric.assessment-close: Explains the complimentary 15–20 minute human-specialist assessment and accurate calendar-to-CRM sequence.
rubric.handoff: Records facts, estimates, unknowns and actual agreements without inventing a solution or meeting.
rubric.ethics: No unauthorized pricing, fabricated claims, contact-restriction bypass or misleading booking.
rubric.accuracy: Every important claim matches the supplied evidence and role boundaries.
